newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-PORTO STAY ON TOP AMID FLURRY OF RED CARDS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PORTO STAY ON TOP AMID FLURRY OF RED CARDS.

text.p: Portuguese champions Porto were held to a surprise 2-2 home draw by struggling Rio Ave on Sunday in a bad-tempered day's fixtures which saw 11 players sent off in five games.

Despite the setback Porto retain a comfortable lead with 67 points, eight ahead of Sporting who beat Gil Vicente 3-0 away on Saturday. Benfica, who beat Espinho 2-0, are in third place with 51 points.

Rio Ave, who took a third minute lead through Emanuel Braga, ended the match with nine men after defenders Edivaldo Peu and Marcos Santos were sent off in the 46th and 68th minutes respectively for a foul and a second bookable offence.

The hosts equalised in the 35th minute with a header from Brazilian striker Mario Jardel but they too lost a defender just before halftime when Sergio Conceicao got his marching orders for fouling Augusto Gama.

Rio Ave regained the lead in the 49th minute with a powerful shot from just outside the area by defender Joaquim Martins but Porto levelled eight minutes from the end with a goal by substitute Rui Barros after a cross from Artur Oliveira.

Benfica's win also came against a side who finished the game with nine men. Espinho defender Carlos Carvalhal was sent off for a foul on Benfica captain Joao Pinto in the 57th minute and Paulo Lino followed shortly after for a foul on winger Edgar Pacheco.
Benfica's latest Brazilian acquisition, striker Valdir Morais, headed home the opening goal in the 13th minute and countryman Valdo Filho netted their second from a penalty following Lino's foul.
Three players were also sent off in sixth-placed Braga's 1-0 home victory over Boavista which was settled by striker Duarte Toni's 19th minute goal.
In the 69th minute Braga's Artur Jorge was dismissed for his second bookable offence and he was followed by the Boavista duo of Bolivian midfielder Edwin Sanchez and Jorge Couto.
